brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Holder for soldering iron while switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Not built. 3D-printed Hex Cluster parts are plastic and not heat-resistant; the configurator checks geometry only and cannot make a heat-proof/waterproof load-bearing holder for a hot iron. Building one would be unsafe (fire/melting risk).

requirements.requirement: Two bins for solder and spare tips
requirements.evidence: Two full-depth bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full on 3-cell base. Dressed with solder-reel props to show solder storage; second bin usable for cold spare tips (stored unpowered/cold only).
Compact 3-cell bench organizer provides bench-top storage for cold soldering consumables; hot-iron part omitted for safety.

finish.summary: Built a safe 3-cell organizer with two full bins for cold storage of solder and spare tips; declined the hot-iron holder as unsafe in 3D-printed plastic. Props show solder reels; bins can hold solder and cold tips.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your hot-tool holder would risk melting — I'll still set up neat, safe storage for solder and spare tips.
